This game actually makes you feel like your hacking, and takes away the extra fluff that make all the boring parts of real life pentesting, and replaces them with fun action sequences that raise the stakes. I played this for way, way longer than my time shows. Me and my old boss used to play this game on our workstations during lunch breaks (I think he got it off GOG though). I know this game is good because I am REALLY bad at it, but yet I still want to play it. I'm on a med that messes with my reactive thinking, so timed events and Quick Time Events mess with me in video games and frustrate the hell out of me. Hacknet is no different with the "trace time" count downs when I'm hacking into systems, but this game is so good that I still come back despite that. 

I also love probing around the computers and seeing weird stories unfold through saved IRC chats and old emails people have on their systems. It's a fun game that teaches you some UNIX commands (no the hacking aspect is not real; this is not a hacking sim) while some banging electronic music puts you in the mood. 

Plus the game is $1.49 cents right now. My coffee at the bodega cost that much this morning (actually, my coffee was a penny more), so yea, this game is worth it. And the Workshop adds a ton of cool stuff to the game.

TLDR. Play this game. Play this game. Play this game. (No spoilers!)

WOW.

You really wouldnt think that a game centered around typing the same commands over and over again would be fun, entertaining, hell, even IMMERSIVE. But you would be dead wrong. 

Hacknet, at its core is a puzzle-narrative game where you like, hack into computers and stuff and do contracts for people, as well as trying to solve a mystery(!!!). It's story is really cool, both the base game AND the DLC (Which is 100 percent worth getting, by the way!). 

I found myself connecting and liking the people who owned these computers I was hacking into, just by reading the little notes they leave, the IRC logs ambiently lying around on their desktop, even the apps they had on their phones. 

The music for this game is INCREDIBLE. Not only does it sound great, but the choice of music for certain/big events actually sent chills down my spine when they first dropped. 

Is this game anything like real life hacking, like the game claims? Hell no. It's super simplified. But, if it wasn't, it wouldn't be fun for tech cavemen like myself.

The game explains its mechanics well, so it's not overwhelming, even if you're unfamiliar with a console. Gameplay consists of typing a few commands and reading in search of whatever piece of information you need to complete the mission. The missions are repetitive by their very nature, but the gameplay is engaging, and it's full of easter eggs, so you do not get bored.

It could have been better streamlined: there are a lot of filler documents, and the plot does not advance until the end of the game; fortunately, it does not overstay its welcome.
